pairs.question: Numquid tamen in hominis necem auctor ista providit?
pairs.answer: Atquin omnem homicidii speciem uno et principali praecepto interimit: "non occides."
pairs.derivation: The author has just said that iron, like herbs and angels, is God's thing (tam ferrum dei res est quam herbae, quam angeli). He then poses the question whether the creator provided these things for the killing of man, and answers it himself with atquin: on the contrary, God abolishes every kind of homicide by the command 'thou shalt not kill.' Question kept whole; answer is the single sentence (to the full stop after non occides) that genuinely answers the question; no framing tag present to strip.

pairs.question: Quid enim, si alio in tempore circum adiero, periclitabor de inquinamento?
pairs.derivation: Author anticipates the reader's objection (introduced de locis ... ad praeveniendam quorundam interrogationem). The framing word inquis ('you say') is dropped per the rules; quid enim is the speaker's own words and kept. The reader asks whether visiting the circus at a non-show time risks pollution; the author answers directly: there is no prescription about places. Answer cut at the first full stop; what follows (nam non sola ista conciliabula ... ) elaborates that even temples may be entered, so it is excluded as digression.
